title: Scenario
description: A scenario config, config/scenarios/<id>.yaml (PRD 4.3, 7.1 FR-INT-11, ADR-0014): the skill set, connectors, seed data, autonomy policy and world theme a scenario preloads, and nothing else. Data only: no code, prompt, model id, brief text or plan, so a scenario that needs any of those becomes a pillar requirement first, and no platform source names a scenario id. The same shape serves any scenario, a demo, a held-out bank case or a generated brief. theme is the world theme, the same slug as layout.schema.json theme (config/themes/, FR-WLD-15; only its shape is checked until that folder exists, BQ-202). Rules that need other files (the id equals the file name, connectors in config/connectors.yaml, seed files exist inside the repo, each autonomy level within its risk tier's max_level, T3 at L1 only) are SN-01 to SN-09 in contracts/scenario.rules.md, checked by the loader.

title.description: Display name of the scenario, plain text.

skills.description: Skill ids the scenario preloads (skills/<domain>/<skill-id>/skill.yaml, FR-AGT-04); at least one.

connectors.description: Connector ids the scenario uses, each declared in config/connectors.yaml (SN-03); may be empty. Preloading a connector never connects it: the person still grants it on a consent card (PRD 10.3, FR-HIL-08).

seed_data.description: Seed files the scenario loads, as repo-relative paths (SN-04); may be empty.

autonomy.description: Policy seeds (PRD 10.4). Each entry becomes one policy.schema.json record only when the owner approves the task, as the owner's own (SN-08); absent or empty preloads none. Each level is at most its action type's max_level in config/autonomy.yaml, so a T3 action never goes above L1 (SN-06).

id.description: Scenario id: a letter, then up to 31 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores. Equals the file name without .yaml (SN-01). The not-pattern rejects a final line break, which a Python validator's $ lets through.

seed_path.description: A repo-relative file path with forward slashes. Each segment starts with a letter, digit or underscore, so there is no absolute path, drive letter, backslash, empty segment, . or .. segment, and no hidden file such as .env or .git. The not-pattern rejects a final line break, which a Python validator's $ lets through.

autonomy_entry.description: One policy seed: the policy.schema.json fields a scenario may set. Everything else is fixed when the policy is created (SN-08): owner and stamps from the approving owner, scope recipients, domains and districts empty, limits.credits null, conditions all true, expiry null, notify_channel web, no Team Lead domains. A scenario never sets a tier: tiers come from config/autonomy.yaml and its modifiers.

connectors.description: The policy's scope.connectors: ids from the scenario's own connectors, or the reserved internal for an action that goes through no connector (SN-07).

per_day.description: The policy's limits.per_day: most actions per UTC day. Required at L2 and L3 (policy.schema.json, BQ-30); left out at L0 and L1 means no daily cap (null in the policy).

undo_window_s.description: The policy's undo_window_s: seconds an L2 action can still be undone; left out means the policy default, 60.

then.description: A policy that acts without a person at the gate needs a daily limit (policy.schema.json).
